name: Independent graders of Situational Awareness — verbatim quotes, mapped to this site's 8 predictions
license: CC BY 4.0 (this compilation); quotes remain their authors' words, quoted for comparison with attribution and link
note: Each grade below is a verbatim sentence from the grader's own public post, read on the date given. The 'label' is this site's editorial mapping of that sentence onto a five-value scale (ahead / on_track / behind / wrong / unresolved) and is the only judgement added here; a reader who disagrees with a mapping can see the sentence it came from. A grader who did not address a prediction has no row for it — silence is never counted as agreement.

scale.ahead: the grader says reality is ahead of the prediction
scale.on_track: the grader says the prediction is being met / checks out
scale.behind: the grader says reality lags the prediction but it has not failed
scale.wrong: the grader says the prediction missed
scale.unresolved: the grader says it cannot be judged yet

graders.author: Nathan Delisle
graders.title: Situational Awareness: A One-Year Retrospective
graders.scope: Quantitative audit of the 'drivers' (compute, algorithmic efficiency, unhobbling) and 'indicators' (cluster size, investment, chips, revenue, electricity) using public data through June 2025. Does not grade AGI-2027, the government project, open source, intelligence explosion or superintelligence.

graders.author: Jamie Harris
graders.title: How did Leopold do? Evaluating Situational Awareness's predictions
graders.scope: Qualitative evaluation across infrastructure, benchmarks, government, agents, revenue, China/US, open source, safety and the AGI-2027 timeline.

graders.author: Daniel Reeves
graders.title: Retrospective Book Review: Situational Awareness
graders.scope: Retrospective by the Beeminder co-founder after a group re-read that started a year after publication 'with the goal of assessing its predictions'. Verdicts are explicitly hedged. Grades knowledge work, the trillion-dollar cluster and the drop-in remote worker on the 2027 timescale; his base-model/unhobbling remark is about capability returns, not the ~0.5 OOM/yr pace, so it is not mapped.

graders.author: Philipp D. Dubach
graders.title: Aschenbrenner's Receipts (Leopold Aschenbrenner Predictions: A Two-Year Scorecard)
graders.scope: Personal-site scorecard dated 21 May 2026 (page shows 'Updated 16 August 2026'). Grades the counting-OOMs framework, nationalisation, open-source diffusion and the 2027-28 window; its GPQA and power sentences address claims this site does not track, so they are listed separately.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: AI capabilities on benchmarks have broadly met his expectations, though the qualitative "shocking leap" hasn't landed as he described.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: Compute, algorithmic efficiency, and unhobbling gains seem to follow Aschenbrenner’s forecasts as well, although with more uncertainty.

grades.label: ahead
grades.quote: Infrastructure investment and algorithmic efficiency are tracking ahead of his predictions.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: Overall, Aschenbrenner’s predicted pace of roughly half an order-of-magnitude annual progress is ~roughly supported by available evidence.

grades.label: ahead
grades.quote: Infrastructure investment and algorithmic efficiency are tracking ahead of his predictions.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: Using publicly available data as of June 2025, this audit finds that global AI investment, electricity consumption, and chip production follow Aschenbrenner’s forecasts.

grades.label: wrong
grades.quote: But he missed that China would innovate independently and that open-source models would thrive at the frontier.

grades.label: unresolved
grades.quote: The AGI-by-2027 timeline is unresolved. It looked implausible six months ago, but recent capability jumps (particularly on software engineering tasks) have made it more credible again.

grades.label: behind
grades.quote: Government response is behind what he predicted, though his AGI project timeline (27/28) hasn't elapsed yet.

grades.label: unresolved
grades.quote: In terms of homework and exams, absolutely. And I don’t think it was obvious in June 2024 how thoroughly true that would be (the International Math Olympiad gold medal performance being the biggest surprise). But Aschenbrenner meant more than homework and exams or even math competitions so there’s plenty of ambiguity about how accurate this prediction is so far.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: And as for the progress toward the trillion-dollar cluster, well, Stargate is happening on schedule. Aschenbrenner doesn’t look particularly wrong with any of his “just trust the trendlines” predictions.

grades.label: unresolved
grades.quote: As for full-fledged AI agents and drop-in remote workers on that timescale, my gut says no, but my gut has said no to a lot of things the past few years that have proceeded to happen.

grades.label: on_track
grades.quote: The framework is unfashionably simple. It is also empirically unusually well calibrated.

grades.label: behind
grades.quote: By May 21, 2026, the full nationalisation that he predicted had not happened.

grades.label: wrong
grades.quote: Bets on defence-AI consolidation and against open-source diffusion would not have paid.

grades.label: unresolved
grades.quote: The strongest counter-counter is that the timeline remained open on May 21, 2026.

not_on_this_site.quote: AI revenue isn't quite as high: he predicted $100B run rate by mid-2026, and the best is $60B.
However, recent OpenAI and Anthropic models trail raw-compute trends by about one-third to one-half an order of magnitude, and AI-related revenue growth is several months behind.
China/US competition intensified as he predicted, and most of his specifics were right (7nm chips, power infrastructure, espionage, CCP waking up, Middle East).
Safety and security remain roughly as inadequate as he described, with his warnings about state-actor exploitation and race-dynamic pressure on safety vindicated.
It took roughly 18 months, almost exactly the prediction window.
His power-not-chips framing preceded consensus and later became industry consensus.
